_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for ITC Hotels (consolidated, Rs crore; company EBITDA definition, see ITCHOTELS.patch.js). Two reported segments: Hotels ex-real estate (rooms, F&B, management fees, other operating revenue; kept in businessLines.hotel and checked against the segment in ITCHOTELS.ctx.js) and Real Estate (Sapphire Residences, Colombo: apartment handovers). Minorities are ~0.4% of profit and sit in the tax rate.

segments.name: Hotels (ex-real estate)
segments._why: Sum of the four streams in businessLines.hotel: rooms +9% / +11% / +9% (Q1FY27 +8% with RevPAR +8%: occupancy +290 bps, rate +4%; FY26 +10%; ~200 acquired keys from Q2-Q3FY27 (Welcomhotel Ahmedabad 130, Kumarakom 72) and ~220 new owned keys in FY28 (Bhubaneswar 118, Puri 100+)), F&B +9% / +10% / +9% (Q1 +11%, FY26 +8%), management fees +25% / +20% / +18% (Q1 +35%, FY26 +28%; the 2.5x-of-FY25 target by FY30 needs ~18% a year from FY26), other operating revenue +12% / +10% / +10% (Q1 +14%, FY26 +18%).
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin ex-real estate FY25 34.0%, FY26 34.6% (+53 bps, +147 bps on a comparable basis), Q1FY27 31.3% (+125 bps YoY in the seasonally weakest quarter). 35.3% / 36.0% / 36.5%: fee mix (fees are almost all margin) and room-rate leverage, partly offset by Kumarakom's renovation and start-up costs and higher energy costs after the West Asia shock.

segments.name: Real estate (Sapphire Residences, Colombo)
segments._why: Revenue is booked when apartments are handed over. FY26 Rs211 cr (Q3 Rs82 cr, Q4 Rs130 cr), Q1FY27 Rs38 cr. Rs160 cr in FY27 (Q1 run-rate plus a stronger H2), then Rs180 cr a year: the AR FY26 says elevated Sri Lankan real-estate taxes have tempered sales momentum. Unsold inventory (Rs1,240 cr at cost, Mar-26) is valued separately in the SOTP.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 EBITDA Rs64 cr on Rs211 cr (30%); Q1FY27 Rs11 cr on Rs38 cr (29%). 30%.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any segment
_unallocWhy: Segments sum to consolidated EBITDA as reported (FY26 Rs1,360 + Rs64 = Rs1,424 cr; Q1FY27 Rs281 + Rs11 = Rs292 cr).

businessLines._why: Hotels ex-real estate build (Rs cr). FY26 base: rooms 1,986, F&B 1,535, management fees 173, others 234 = 3,928 (Q4FY26 deck slide 16). Growth per stream in segments[0]._why.

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits with more than 12 months' maturity reported in other non-current financial assets (AR FY26 consolidated note 6: Rs528.50 cr). With Screener's cash (Rs765 cr) and investments (Rs1,956 cr incl. Rs126 cr of associates at equity) gross treasury is Rs3,250 cr; less Rs74 cr of borrowings (leases) = Rs3,175 cr net cash at Mar-26.

_capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs410 cr, FY25 Rs386 cr (cash flow statement). Management: 10-12% of cumulative revenue for operating capex, renovations, new builds and expansions (Q1FY27 deck slide 24). FY27E Rs950 cr = ~Rs480 cr organic (~11% of revenue) + The Zuri Kumarakom (Rs205 cr EV, completed 19-May-2026) + Welcomhotel Ahmedabad (GHK, Rs155 cr EV, expected in Q2FY27) + ~Rs110 cr (about a third) of the Rs326.5 cr Yashobhoomi land premium (timing not disclosed). Acquisitions are put in capex because the engine has no acquisition line; their cash leaves net cash either way. FY28-29E Rs650 cr: ~12-13% of revenue as Vizag (Rs328 cr approved), Puri, Bhubaneswar and New Delhi are built.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs417 cr = 3.9% of average gross block (Rs10,742 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs104 cr (Rs416 cr annualised).
_treasuryWhy: Zero: treasury income is built in otherIncome (see ITCHOTELS.ctx.js).
_otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 consolidated note 25 (Rs192 cr): interest Rs162 cr (bank deposits Rs115 cr, bonds at amortised cost Rs46 cr) + fair-value and sale gains on mutual funds Rs27 cr + other Rs3 cr, on ~Rs2,700 cr average gross treasury = ~7%; plus share of associates (International Travel House 48.96%, Maharaja Heritage Resorts JV) Rs12 cr. FY27E: ~6.75% on ~Rs3,200 cr average treasury (Mar-26 Rs3,250 cr, less ~Rs500 cr of acquisitions and land premium, plus free cash) = ~Rs216 cr + associates ~Rs14 cr = Rs230 cr (Q1FY27: other income Rs59 cr + associates Rs4 cr = Rs63 cr, x4 = Rs252 cr). Then +Rs25-30 cr a year as cash builds. Excludes exceptional items.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs7.93 cr (lease interest Rs6.58 cr; no bank debt), Q1FY27 Rs2 cr.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine has no minority line). FY26 before exceptional items: tax Rs302 cr on PBT Rs1,203 cr = 25.1%; reported 26.9%; Q1FY27 Rs66 cr on Rs249 cr = 26.5%; minorities ~0.3-0.4% of PBT (FY26 Rs4 cr; Q1FY27 Rs2 cr). 26.8%.
_payoutWhy: First dividend: Rs1 a share for FY26 (Rs208 cr) = 25% of reported EPS (Rs3.92).

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash and no debt, so the 12.2% cost of equity is the discount rate; beta 0.95 as for IHCL: hotel demand is cyclical (Covid, West Asia) but there is no financial leverage.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian travel and hotel spending grows with nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house range (as IHCL).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 36%: hotel margin near FY29E with a growing fee share; real estate fades out.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from ~12% of revenue to 9%: renovation ~5% plus owned growth keys (5,700 owned keys today, ~7,500 by 2031).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: West Asia normalises by H2FY27, RevPAR grows ~9-10% a year, management fees reach 2.5x FY25 a year early, Kumarakom, Ahmedabad and Puri ramp fast and the market pays the top quartile of ITC Hotels' own post-listing multiple range after the same sector move.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 2026 travel shock lingers: inbound and MICE stay weak, RevPAR grows ~4-5%, energy and staff costs squeeze margins, Sapphire sales stall under Sri Lankan property taxes and the stock stays at the bottom quartile of its range after the sector de-rating.

parts.name: Hotels (owned and managed)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E hotel EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Company EBITDA ex-real estate; multiple derived in the valuation chapter.

parts.name: Sapphire Residences: unsold inventory at book less 20%
parts.metricLabel: Rs1,240 cr inventory at cost (Mar-26) × 0.8 (bull 0.9, bear 0.7)
parts.note: Cash still to come from apartments not yet handed over; the margin on units handed over by Sep-28E is in our EBITDA and net cash.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-28E (cash, investments and long deposits less leases)
parts.note: Mar-26: Rs3,250 cr gross treasury (incl. Rs126 cr associates at book) less Rs74 cr leases = Rs3,175 cr.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA)
methods.why: How the street values ITC Hotels: EV/EBITDA on FY28E (see the street table).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings: own forward P/E median since 1-Apr-2025 adjusted for the hotel peers' P/E move over the same window.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, 12.2% discount rate, 6% terminal growth, plus net cash.
